To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

StoRM can be successfully used to manage GPFS file systems and that StoRM is capable of providing a throughput of up to about 1 GB/s for single file transfers, and of about 1.2 GB/s for concurrent transfers, when using a 10 Gb/s network.
StoRM is a very stable system, able to manage a large number of data volumes and to serve a large number of concurrent clients with high throughput.
StoRM can be configured to work well with the GPFS parallel file system and that StoRM can handle high throughput rates, but it is limited in the number of concurrent users.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) How does the StoRM SRM perform under heavy load? (b) What are the performance characteristics of the StoRM SRB? and (c) What is the throughput of the StoRM storage backend?
the performance of StoRM and its ability to scale in order to manage a large amount of storage.
the performance and scalability of StoRM and its interaction with GPFS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
StoRM is a very stable and robust SRM, and that it can be used to manage a GPfs file system in a grid environment.
StoRM is a very promising solution for managing large disk storage resources, and it is a very valuable tool for the management of the data volumes of the CERN data centres.
StoRM is able to handle the expected number of requests and to provide the expected performance for a large number of concurrent users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
StoRM can be successfully integrated with GPFS and that it is possible to achieve a good performance for the StoRM server.
StoRM is an efficient and reliable SRM for the GPFS file system, and that StoRM can scale to large number of files and large number of users.
StoRM can manage a GPFS-based storage system in a grid environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
StoRM can be configured to provide the required SRM functionality, with acceptable performance, to a SAN-oriented parallel file system such as GPFS.
StoRM can be successfully deployed on top of GPFS, with a throughput comparable with the one of a native GPFS client.
, with the current implementation of StoRM, the SRM interface is not the main bottleneck of the system.
